newsitem.title: MEXICO: Avantel seeks 6-8 pct of Mexico long-distance mart.
newsitem.headline: Avantel seeks 6-8 pct of Mexico long-distance mart.

text.p: Mexican telecommunications company Avantel hopes to hold national long-distance market share of between six percent and eight percent, company President Roberto Hernandez said Friday.
"In the first stage, for the first two years, we are focusing on a share of between six and eight percent," he said in a press conference at the presidential residence Los Pinos.
Hernandez said he told Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo in a private meeting that the company has spent $900 million to build "the most modern fiber-optic network in the world."
Competition in telephone services started in August for business clients and will be extended to residential customers on January 1.
Avantel is a joint venture between MCI Communications Corp and Banamex-Accival, Mexico's largest bank.
